transcript:
Agent: Thank you for calling card member services. How can I assist you today?
Customer: Hi, I'm calling because there has been fraud committed on my card, and I need it taken care of immediately.
Agent: I can certainly look into that for you. May I please have your full name and your billing zip code to pull up your file?
Customer: Yes, my name is Rafael Sutter, and the zip code is 97201.
Agent: Thank you, Mr. Sutter. Could you tell me which charge you are calling about, including the merchant and the amount?
Customer: It's from Skyward Air. There is a $189.00 charge, well, actually two of them, and one of them is absolute fraud.
Agent: I see two charges from Skyward Air on your account. What was the date of the transaction you're looking at?
Customer: It happened on September 2nd. I was looking through everything and noticed two identical charges on the same day.
Agent: Can you tell me a little more about what you purchased with Skyward Air on September 2nd?
Customer: I was flying with them and decided to pay for a seat upgrade. It was just one upgrade for my flight.
Agent: And both of the items on your account show for $189.00 on September 2nd?
Customer: Yes, exactly. I agreed to one upgrade for $189.00, but they hit my card a second time for $189.00. That second one is straight-up fraud.
Agent: Did you receive any confirmation emails or receipts from the airline when you completed the purchase?
Customer: I got one confirmation email with one receipt showing the single seat selection for $189.00. Nothing else.
Agent: Have you had a chance to speak with Skyward Air directly regarding the two transactions?
Customer: I tried, but their phone line had an endless wait, and nobody answered my message. That's why I'm calling you to report the fraud.
Agent: Did anyone else have permission to use your card or make changes to your flight reservation?
Customer: No, nobody else. I was traveling alone, and I'm the only person with access to the card.
Agent: Let me make sure I have all the details noted correctly. On September 2nd, you purchased a single seat upgrade from Skyward Air for $189.00, received one confirmation, but two separate charges of $189.00 appeared from that merchant on that date.
Customer: That's right. The first one was mine, but that second one is total fraud.
